routines.semantics: Returns ET minus UTC in seconds at an epoch expressed as formal UTC or ET seconds past J2000. Epoch scale matters near a leap boundary; UTC and ET queries are not interchangeable inputs. Both uppercase selectors are the existing typed contract. Required LSK/relativistic variables must be present.

scenarios.observes: Every actual delta scalar reaches live comparison for both input scales, nonzero positive/negative epochs and pre/post leap steps. The result is near 60 seconds rather than a large epoch baseline, preserving sensitivity under existing tolerance. Case: Computes ET-UTC delta at J2000 ET with LSK loaded

routines.edgeAssessment: Returns ET minus UTC in seconds at an epoch expressed as formal UTC or ET seconds past J2000. Epoch scale matters near a leap boundary; UTC and ET queries are not interchangeable inputs. Both uppercase selectors are the existing typed contract. Required LSK/relativistic variables must be present. The synthetic clock has small exact tick/epoch values, two partitions and a shared endpoint, so it exercises precision/indexing beyond one real-clock sample. Same-instance integration tests recover after clock/UTC errors; string/selector/numeric boundaries are tested separately.
routines.errorAssessment: Registered error cases require actual specific CSPICE codes: missing SCLK/LSK variables, INVALIDTIMEFORMAT, MISSINGTIMEINFO, VALUEOUTOFRANGE, BADPARTNUMBER, EMPTYSTRING or YEAROUTOFRANGE as applicable. The initial exact-input oracle probe corrected an assumed NOLEAPSECONDS name to actual et2utc MISSINGTIMEINFO rather than weakening the assertion. Fractional/wrapped integer parameters, non-string JS inputs and unsupported uppercase-contract selectors are adapter validation, not CSPICE diagnostic equivalence. Output-buffer null/truncation/partition-capacity flooding is not fabricated through unsafe descriptors; temporary allocation rollback is fault-injected.

routines.fixtureRationale: Existing real-clock/LSK smoke inputs are retained. New synthetic clock constants are authored, minimal, deterministic and explicitly documented; they model no real spacecraft. Both ET and conditional non-TDB correlation paths execute actual CSPICE rather than a harness clock model.
routines.cleanup: Each case registers kernel ownership, unloads/clears kernel pool and resets errors on success/failure. Clock watcher invalidation is exercised by fresh/missing metadata cases in the shared native process; no pool data escapes a case. Direct tests dispose clients and verify a bad partition/UTC error is followed by successful work on the same backend. All 20 temporary allocation failure positions release earlier strings/error/output buffers.
routines.tolerance: No tolerance changes. Complete clock/calendar strings compare exactly, including era/partition/rounding. New synthetic clock values are small binary-exact fractions, so existing 1e-12 absolute/relative comparison detects fractional tick/partition/normalization defects. Legacy large real-clock values retain the existing relative tolerance and are supplemented by the small-clock cases; UTC delta outputs stay near 60 seconds.

findings.summary: Original success evidence used one epoch/one cookbook clock, leaving constant results, partition handling, fractional rounding or epoch-dependent delta insufficiently distinguished.
findings.repair: Add multiple distinguishing UTC epochs or an authored small two-partition clock, compare every actual scalar/string, and require named relevant diagnostics. Keep live SpiceyPy as oracle, without fixture-derived substitute outputs.
